title: Synthetic RNA-seq Quality Control Playbook
text:
Before accepting a sequencing run, review read quality, adapter contamination, mapping behavior, duplication, and predefined sample-level acceptance criteria. Quality checks should be interpreted together rather than relying on a single metric.

If a sample fails a predefined threshold, record the reason, preserve the raw evidence, and route the sample for review instead of silently excluding it. The acceptance decision and any override should be auditable.

title: Synthetic Scientific ML Evaluation Guide
text:
A model evaluation set should be separated from training and model-selection data. For imbalanced scientific classification problems, report metrics that reflect minority-class performance in addition to aggregate discrimination.

Regression tests should use a fixed evaluation set and explicit release thresholds. A model change should not be promoted simply because one headline metric improves if calibration, subgroup behavior, latency, or operational failure rates regress.

title: Synthetic Evidence Assistant Operating Policy
text:
An evidence assistant should cite the passages supporting its answer and abstain when retrieval does not provide adequate support. Source identifiers should be stable enough to reproduce the evidence shown to a user.

Operational logs should capture request identifiers, latency, retrieval counts, model or pipeline version, and error state. Sensitive document contents should not be copied into logs by default.

title: Synthetic Assay Operations Note
text:
Assay workflows benefit from explicit acceptance criteria, versioned protocols, and traceable deviations. When a process changes, teams should document what changed and evaluate whether the change affects downstream interpretation.

A human review step is appropriate when automated checks are inconclusive or when a result falls close to a decision boundary.
